As traditional giants rush into digital dollars, USDD’s Yvonne Chia explains why 24/7 access, self-custody, and transparent yield give decentralized stablecoins an edge banks can’t replicate.

20 November – Road Town, Totorla, British Virgin Islands – Decentralized stablecoin protocol USDD is accelerating its multichain utility across TRON, Ethereum, and BNB Chain—combining automated sUSDD yield via its Smart Allocator with GasFree zero-TRX transfers—as traditional financial giants race to build competing stablecoin rails.

In a recent industry interview with instant exchange partner ChangeNOW, USDD Head of Communications Yvonne Chia outlined why self-custody, 24/7 settlement, and transparent onchain reserves give decentralized digital dollars a structural advantage over bank-issued alternatives.

For billions of people globally, opening and maintaining a traditional bank account still involves paperwork, minimum balance requirements, geographic restrictions, and approval delays. Even when banks integrate stablecoin rails behind the scenes, those services remain gated behind legacy compliance walls and intermediary control.

Crypto-native stablecoins flip that model on its head. As Yvonne Chia highlighted during the interview:

“Compare this to a stablecoin like USDD, where all you need is a phone, a working internet connection, you can immediately start a wallet and you have access to your funds right away.”

With USDD, users can access and manage their digital dollars directly through their own wallets, without depending on traditional financial intermediaries.

This represents a fundamental shift in financial access: users are no longer limited to the services, operating hours, or account structures of a single institution. Instead, they have the freedom to hold, manage, and transfer their assets on their own terms.

Self-custody also gives users greater autonomy over their financial decisions. They can choose which wallets to use, where to transfer their assets, and which supported decentralized applications to interact with, without needing to route every transaction through a centralized financial institution.

With USDD, users’ digital dollars can move with them across an open blockchain ecosystem, rather than remaining tied to a particular bank or service provider.

Legacy payment networks still operate on decades-old schedules: weekend cutoffs, bank holidays, and multi-day cross-border settlement delays accompanied by hefty wire fees.

Blockchain networks never close. Whether it is a Sunday night or a public holiday, USDD moves globally without depending on traditional banking operating hours or settlement windows.

“We are able to have transfers 24/7 and we’re not limited to any traditional banking hours. So I think that in some ways, stablecoins are not just becoming banks, but exceeding what traditional banks can offer to users.”

To make everyday transfers even smoother than fintech apps, USDD introduced GasFree integration on TRON, allowing users on supported wallets to pay network fees directly in USDD without needing to hold TRX.

This removes another practical barrier to stablecoin adoption: having to acquire and maintain a separate gas token just to transfer digital dollars. With GasFree, eligible users can pay approximately 0.5 USDD per transaction, compared with around 1.5 USDT for a standard USDT transfer under the referenced fee conditions.

These improvements matter because the usefulness of a stablecoin is not determined by its peg alone. Low-cost transfers, straightforward wallet experiences, and around-the-clock availability are what make digital dollars practical for everyday payments and global value transfers.

Perhaps the sharpest contrast between banks and decentralized stablecoins lies in how yield is distributed.

In traditional banking, institutions take customer deposits, deploy them into yield-generating markets, and retain a significant portion of the returns. Everyday depositors may receive relatively low interest rates, while higher-yielding products often come with eligibility requirements, minimum deposits, or fixed maturity periods.

Stablecoins introduce another way to participate in digital-dollar opportunities. Rather than keeping capital entirely within a traditional deposit account, users can access onchain yield opportunities through decentralized protocols and transparent investment mechanisms.

USDD was built to return that value directly to holders. Through USDD Earn, users can deposit USDD to receive sUSDD, earning automated, competitive yield powered by our Smart Allocator system, with no fixed lock-up periods restricting access to their capital.

For users, the distinction is important: USDD Earn provides access to a productive stablecoin while maintaining flexibility, rather than requiring users to commit their capital to a conventional fixed-term product.

Traditional banks ask customers to trust closed-door balance sheets and periodic regulatory filings—until a crisis proves otherwise.

USDD takes a different approach through its “Don’t trust, verify” ethos, emphasizing publicly accessible onchain information and independent verification.

Transparency does not eliminate financial or technical risks, but it changes how users can evaluate them. Instead of relying exclusively on an institution’s assurances, users have access to information that can be independently examined and verified.

The bigger picture is an interconnected financial ecosystem in which users can move between holding, transferring, exchanging, and deploying their stablecoins according to their own needs. These are not isolated functions. Together, they make stablecoins more useful as everyday financial infrastructure.

Banks will undoubtedly continue using stablecoin rails to modernize their back-end settlement. However, true financial freedom comes from open networks where assets flow freely across protocols without intermediaries.

For USDD, the opportunity goes beyond offering a dollar-pegged asset. It is about making digital dollars accessible, transferable, and productive across an interconnected financial ecosystem. From self-custody and 24/7 transfers to flexible yield opportunities and multichain DeFi access, these capabilities give users more ways to put their money to work.

Banks may be bringing stablecoins into traditional finance. Crypto-native protocols are showing what stablecoins can make possible beyond it.

#5141. GTA VI Launch Sparks $250M Solana Stock Frenzy Over Nvidia

Home » Altcoins » Solana (SOL) » GTA VI Launch Sparks $250M Solana Stock Frenzy Over Nvidia

Tokenized Take-Two shares saw a massive 24-hour trading spike as on-chain markets attract Washington scrutiny.

The long-awaited release of Grand Theft Auto VI didn’t just break gaming records—it briefly turned publisher Take-Two Interactive into the hottest stock on the blockchain, outselling even AI giant Nvidia.

On November 18, decentralized exchange (DEX) trading volume for tokenized Take-Two shares (TTWO) exploded by 578%, jumping from $36.8 million to $249.5 million in a single day, according to Token Terminal data.

That was roughly 2.8 times the $88.1 million traded in tokenized Nvidia (NVDA) shares over the same 24-hour window, accounting for 42% of all on-chain stock trading.

Nearly all of the action, roughly $239 million, or 96% of total volume, happened on Solana via Backpack Securities, a subsidiary of crypto exchange Backpack. Launched earlier this year, the token is designed to be backed 1:1 by real Take-Two shares held in custody.

Traditional Wall Street traders saw a much calmer reaction: Take-Two’s Nasdaq shares rose 6.2% to close at $216.61 on launch day before pulling back 3.7% to $208.65 the next session.

Despite Take-Two’s one-day viral spike, Nvidia remains the undisputed heavyweight of tokenized equities, boasting a $399.4 million market cap and $2 billion in 30-day trading volume (compared to Take-Two’s $808.1 million).

Overall, tokenized public stocks on Solana have nearly doubled since late October to reach $1.22 billion.

That rapid growth is drawing fresh scrutiny in Washington. On November 16, four Democratic senators sent a letter to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) questioning how its newly introduced exemption for tokenized securities would address investor protection and anti-money laundering requirements.

The issue also surfaced during the November 19 Senate Banking Committee confirmation hearing for Kristin Johnson, President Donald Trump’s nominee for the SEC. Johnson indicated that exemptions covering tokenized stocks should eventually be formalized through rules following a public comment period.

The TTWO spike shows tokenized stocks can attract event-driven trading on-chain, comparable to some of the largest names in the segment. It also coincides with growing regulatory scrutiny of how tokenized stocks are supervised.

#5138. XRP on Track to Post Worst ETF Month Ever

The XRP ETF market might be bracing to close a record-breaking month of outflows as demand for the XRP-based investment product has remained on hold all through the month.

This comes as the prolonged and intense market volatility has extended to the ETF ecosystem, causing institutional investors to withdraw their capital.

With November just about three weeks gone, the latest data from SoSoValue shows that XRP ETFs have already recorded a total of $30.76 million in net outflows this November.

Previous ETF data shows that March remains the only month in which spot XRP ETFs have recorded net outflows since their launch.

While it still stands as the record outflow month for XRP ETFs, investors withdrew about $31.16 million from the funds during that month.

This means that the persistent withdrawals seen this month have brought the November outflow dangerously close to its previous monthly record seen in March.

Apparently, the spot XRP ETFs are on track to close November as their worst-performing month since launch, with just about $1 million left to hit the record.

Further data also shows that the spot XRP ETFs have yet to record a single day of net inflows throughout November, as the persistent price decline has caused investors to slow down their purchases.

As such, the influx of fresh capital into the spot XRP ETF market has remained on hold amid growing market uncertainty and a shift in investor sentiment.

#5137. Ledger Confirms Tampered Bitcoin Wallets in Berlin as Spy Implant Probe Spreads Beyond Asia

Ledger Confirms Tampered Bitcoin Wallets in Berlin as Spy Implant Probe Spreads Beyond Asia

The tampered Ledger wallets aren’t just a Southeast Asia problem anymore.

Ledger said Wednesday it has confirmed tampered hardware wallets in Berlin and is investigating reports of two more in Dubai, expanding a probe it had previously described as a localized incident in Southeast Asia.

“Our findings since then show tampered devices outside Southeast Asia. It is the same incident,” the company said in an update on its support site.

The investigation began last month after customers who bought devices from reseller CryptoBilis reported losses. Onchain investigators traced a suspected drain of about $87 million from hundreds of victim wallets across Ethereum, Tron, and Bitcoin.

Ledger said at the time that all confirmed cases were tied to CryptoBilis, and it later asked resellers in seven Asian markets to pull devices from sale.

Every device Ledger has confirmed shows the same kind of physical modification, designed to capture a user’s recovery phrase during setup. A recovery phrase, typically a string of 24 words, is the master key to a crypto wallet: anyone who has it can drain the funds.

Our investigation into the hardware implant incident we disclosed Oct 15th is ongoing, and we published an update: https://t.co/wx6mfQPr99

There is no flaw in Ledger's secure chip or operating system, and no confirmed case involving a device bought on https://t.co/vQ4QWa1D0f

Ledger maintains there’s no flaw in its secure chip or operating system and no confirmed case involving a device bought on ledger.com.

In Germany, Ledger said a few tampered units were localized to Berlin, and it urged anyone who bought a Ledger device there since January 2026 to contact support.

In Dubai, it’s working with distribution partners to learn how two suspected units entered circulation. Those devices were bought at a Virgin Megastore location, according to multiple reports. Ledger also found one affected Nano Gen5 among the Southeast Asian resellers it previously paused.

The company expects more tampered devices to surface, though it says the number remains small overall. Its Donjon security team is examining suspected devices, and Ledger has asked resellers to pause sales wherever inspections are ongoing.

Customers worried about a device should stop using it, Ledger said. It advises moving funds to a new wallet created on a device bought directly from ledger.com, without reusing the old recovery phrase or passphrase, since a tampered device can capture both. It also recommends filing a report with local authorities.

For a limited time, Ledger is offering physical inspections, including X-rays, at its factory in Vierzon, France.

“We will never ask for your recovery phrase,” the company said on X.

The last few months have been a rough stretch for hardware wallet markers overall. Rival manufacturer Trezor said this week that hackers who breached a third-party shipping partner likely took information tied to about 27,000 orders. That’s the company’s third such breach in as many months.

#5136. Coinbase could claim a betting floor of their own, but what about Kalshi?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Coinbase wants a piece of the prediction markets action, with the exchange reportedly planning a launch next year.

Right now, they don’t run their own; they borrow them. Users trade event contracts on the exchange through a Kalshi partnership. That could change next year though.

Citing sources close to the matter, a Bloomberg report claimed that Coinbase wants to roll out its own event contracts in the U.S in H1 2027. It would be open to both retail and institutional traders.

But why bother? For starters, Coinbase gets to decide what launches and when. Next, it keeps a bigger share of the trading fees.

There’s real money at stake here. In Q3 2026, Coinbase’s prediction markets business was already on track to bring in over $200 million a year. If you think about it, this isn’t an overnight decision. In the run up to it all, Coinbase announced that it was buying prediction market startup The Clearing Company in December 2025.

Then, in September this year, the CFTC gave the green light for its own clearing house.

All that being said, nothing’s set in stone. However, the pieces are clearly falling into place.

Crypto trading may have slowed down, but prediction markets have kept themselves out of the bleeding.

Since launch, revenue from the business has grown by 82% QoQ on average. In Q3 alone, daily traders went up by over 60%, compared to the quarter before.

CFO Alesia Haas summed up the appeal pretty neatly. She said,

Prediction markets are adding another revenue stream and are less correlated to crypto volatility…

A big deal for an exchange that lives and dies by market cycles.

On the earnings call, Haas also said that the new clearing house would let Coinbase run its own contracts and earn more from them.

Worth pointing out, however, that Kalshi isn’t being cut out as partner contracts will stay on the platform.

#5133. Best Hyperliquid trading bots: AI agents and bots compared

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Hyperliquid has become one of the busiest venues for crypto perpetual futures, and a long list of tools now automate trading on it. They differ less in what they promise than in two practical questions: who decides the trades, and what the tool is allowed to do with your account. This guide compares the main Hyperliquid trading bots and AI trading agents in 2026, plus Hyperliquid’s vaults, against those questions. Each tool was compared on who decides the trades, what its key can do with your account, and what evidence of performance exists, using each provider’s own documentation in October 2026.

Most Hyperliquid tools connect through an API wallet, which Hyperliquid also calls an agent wallet. The account owner approves a separate key that can sign orders for the account but cannot withdraw or transfer funds. These approvals expire, and approving a new wallet under the same name replaces the old one. Some tools also recommend a sub-account, which keeps the bot’s balances and positions separate. The assets stay in the user’s own Hyperliquid account throughout, which is why most Hyperliquid bots can fairly be called non-custodial.

Many tools charge through a builder fee, a small fee added to each filled order. It applies only after the user approves a maximum fee from the main wallet, and Hyperliquid caps it at 0.1% on perpetuals.

Tools are grouped by who supplies the trading logic: a managed model first, then signal execution, rule-based bots and open-source software (3Commas sits with the rule-based bots). Vaults come last because they replace a bot rather than run one. Hyperliquid’s own trading and funding fees apply to every option.

AlphaNet is built for Hyperliquid and supplies the trading logic itself. Users pick one of its deep learning strategies for crypto perpetual futures and an allocation, and the model decides when to enter and exit each trade. It connects the way the exchange intends: the user approves an agent wallet that can place and cancel orders but cannot withdraw or transfer, and trades run from the user’s own account. New deployments allow leverage up to 3× account equity. On cost, AlphaNet’s Hyperliquid trading bot charges no platform fee during the current promotional period, compared with builder fees of 0.035–0.1% per fill on several bots below; Hyperliquid’s protocol fees still apply, and a dynamic trading fee applies afterwards.

A newer group of AI agent projects on Hyperliquid connect language models to an API wallet and let them place trades. They are mostly early. In the first season of Alpha Arena, a short real-money competition on Hyperliquid, four of the six language models that took part finished with losses and two with gains.

WunderTrading is built for traders whose strategy already exists as TradingView alerts or external signals. It turns those alerts into Hyperliquid orders and also offers DCA and grid bots, charging a 0.035% builder fee with no separate subscription.

goodcryptoX is a no-code app for grid, DCA, trailing, and TradingView bots on iOS, Android, and the web. Gainium covers similar bot types and adds backtesting and paper trading, with a choice between a free mode that adds a builder fee and paid plans that do not. Bitsgap brings its hosted grid and DCA bots to Hyperliquid alongside the centralised exchanges it already supports, and 3Commas, one of the most widely used bot platforms, lists Hyperliquid among its supported exchanges for spot and futures. With all of them, the bot executes your logic; the tool does not supply a trading edge.

Hummingbot has Hyperliquid spot and perpetual connectors and includes market-making scripts and arbitrage, TWAP, and grid executors. The self-run client charges no builder fee. It accepts either an API wallet or the main wallet’s private key; the second gives the software full control of the account, so the API wallet is the safer choice.

Rule-based bots have no platform-level record, because results depend on each user’s settings. Vaults are the most transparent option: every vault’s history is on-chain and visible in Hyperliquid’s app. Managed strategy platforms sit in between. AlphaNet publishes a running record of each strategy since its start date, and because trades run from users’ own accounts, each user’s fills are on-chain and can be checked against it.

Instead of connecting a tool to your own account, you deposit into a vault that a leader trades. The protocol’s own vault, HLP, provides liquidity, performs liquidations, and earns a share of fees. User-run vaults follow individual strategies. Leaders take 10% of profits and must keep at least 5% of the vault, and deposits are locked for one day (four days for HLP).

The choice comes down to the two questions this guide started with. First, decide who you want making the trades: your own rules, a signal you already trust, a trained model, or a vault leader. Then check what the tool is allowed to do with your account. On Hyperliquid, most tools need only an agent wallet that can trade but not withdraw, so there is rarely a reason to hand over a main wallet key or move funds into someone else’s control.

Two further checks are worth making before committing real capital. The first is cost per fill: builder fees on top of Hyperliquid’s own fees can add up. The second is the record: a vault’s history is on-chain, a managed strategy should publish a live one, and a rule-based bot has none until you build your own.

#5132. Binance can hold MEXC deposits even after the blockchain clears them

MEXC is still processing billions in trades, but Binance's new restrictions show how quickly customers can lose the ability to move their money.

You can send crypto from MEXC to Binance, see that the transaction went through on the blockchain, and still be unable to trade with that deposit when you log in to Binance.

That's what Binance told customers to expect while it reviews deposits from MEXC. Try to move money the other way, and Binance says it'll refuse to send it in the first place.

The US order barring covered US financial institutions from sending or receiving funds involving MEXC takes effect Dec. 10, but Binance announced its policy a month earlier and cited the Treasury's finding.

MEXC can keep matching buy and sell orders in the markets it still serves, while one of the world's largest exchanges has already told traders it will restrict what they can move between the two.

On Nov. 6, the Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) found that MEXC was a foreign financial institution of primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance.

The agency acted under Section 9714 of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act, and its order in the Federal Register prohibits transfers to and from MEXC through covered US financial institutions.

The prohibition has no scheduled end and covers MEXC's foreign operations and successor entities. It reaches crypto as well as conventional money, and FinCEN names Bitcoin explicitly.

Foreign financial firms can make dollar payments through banks that hold accounts with US banks, an arrangement known as correspondent banking.

FinCEN considered restricting those accounts but concluded that doing so would leave other kinds of transfers untouched. Instead, it chose to prohibit transfers that pass through a covered institution, even when MEXC has no account with the institution handling the payment.

Exchanges and payment providers outside that group may adopt their own restrictions, but those policies require separate confirmation.

FinCEN estimates that MEXC handled at least $16.7 billion in likely illicit activity in the five years through May 2026. The agency's figures include about $129 million it says MEXC directly facilitated with Garantex after the Russian crypto exchange was sanctioned, and about $4.1 million involving its successor, Grinex, after it too was sanctioned.

FinCEN also cites transfers linked to Iran and North Korea, along with proceeds from cybercrime. The agency acknowledges that legitimate customers use MEXC and says the financial risks it identified warrant restricting transfers involving the exchange itself.

In its Nov. 7 public response, MEXC said it was operating normally, and customer assets remained secure. It said it had opened an independent review of its anti-money-laundering and sanctions controls and intended to engage with regulators.

Reports noted net outflows from tracked MEXC wallets after the announcement.

Binance can refuse to send a withdrawal because it controls the account the money would leave.

Yet, when crypto comes from another platform, the network can process the transaction without asking the recipient's permission.

FinCEN acknowledges that limitation in the order, and Binance's notice shows what the exchange can do once the funds arrive: it can withhold credit while it reviews the transfer and potentially restrict or close the customer's Binance account.

Any funds left at MEXC stay in that account unless the customer moves them separately.

An on-chain confirmation and exchange-account credit are separate events. Binance says deposits from MEXC entities are withheld for review, while outgoing requests are declined.

Blockchain settlement does not force a receiving exchange to credit a customer balance.

Binance describes platform policy, not a documented individual incident. FinCEN binds covered US financial institutions. A confirmed blockchain transaction does not guarantee immediate account credit; account restrictions are possible, not certain.

Based on the Binance notice published November 10, 2026, and the FinCEN order published November 10 with a December 10 effective date. Inbound path is illustrative; no verified individual customer transfer is claimed.

Binance describes platform policy, not a documented individual incident. FinCEN binds covered US financial institutions. A confirmed blockchain transaction does not guarantee immediate account credit; account restrictions are possible, not certain.

The business risk for exchanges becomes more serious if customers and professional market makers, the firms that keep buy and sell orders available, lose more ways to fund their accounts or move out the proceeds.

Moving balances between exchanges is part of how those firms keep money available where they need it.

MEXC says changes at third-party issuers ended its Asia-Pacific card program on Nov. 11 and its Global Card on Nov. 18.

Global Card customers can no longer use their cards for purchases. MEXC says it will credit balances left on the cards to customers' spot accounts within three business days of a Nov. 21 snapshot.

That would leave customers with an exchange balance rather than a working payment card, because spending it with a card requires an issuer.

In France, MEXC had announced its wind-down in October, before the Treasury acted. Its schedule for French accounts stopped euro deposits and withdrawals on Nov. 18, while crypto withdrawals remain available until March 5, 2027.

Trading restrictions begin in batches, and French accounts enter withdrawal-only mode on Jan. 25.

On Nov. 20, DefiLlama displayed more than $1 billion in MEXC spot trading over 24 hours. That figure measures trading across the platform, including customers outside France, and says little about whether an individual French account can accept deposits, place new orders, or withdraw its remaining funds.

After Dec. 10, the practical reach of FinCEN's order will depend partly on which banks and exchanges handle a trader's money and which restrictions those firms apply.

Binance has already told customers how it intends to handle MEXC transfers. Other firms may take different approaches, which traders will discover when they try to withdraw a balance, deposit it somewhere else, or spend it through a payment service.

Timmer's viewpoint seems to align with that of veteran trader Peter Brandt, who noted that Bitcoin might have entered a "dicey" price range owing to its recent drop. "The territory below this level gets very dicey," he said, underlining the $57,803 price point for Bitcoin.

#5130. Bitcoin Struggles to Hold $64,000 as ETF Outflows Hit $2.9B in November

Bitcoin Struggles to Hold $64,000 as ETF Outflows Hit $2.9B in November

Bitcoin is struggling to hold the $64,000 level as investors continue to pull money from spot Bitcoin ETFs and brace for another interest rate hike from the Federal Reserve.

The leading cryptocurrency was trading at around $63,800 on Thursday, down 1% on the day and 13% over the past week, according to Decrypt data. It has hovered between roughly $63,000 and $65,000 since the weekend, briefly dipping below $63,000 and touching a 24-hour low of $62,068, per CoinGecko data.

"Bitcoin remains under selling pressure," Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com, told Decrypt, noting that it has fallen roughly 26% from its late-September peak near $87,000. "Elevated Treasury yields, dollar strength and expectations of further Fed tightening are weighing on risk appetite, while the broader technology selloff has added to the pressure."

U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $306.4 million in net outflows on Wednesday, after $239.9 million on Tuesday, according to SoSoValue data. The funds have seen outflows on nine of the past 10 trading days, with Monday's small $8 million inflow the only exception, and have lost about $2.9 billion so far in November. Their total net assets have fallen to $77.7 billion. Bitcoin miners have added to the selling, with major miners including Riot and MARA selling some of their holdings to fund a shift into AI infrastructure.

Monday's brief inflow "does not signal a market inflection point," Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey, told Decrypt. Net short positions in Bitcoin futures held by leveraged funds on CME have fallen to their lowest level since early 2023, and futures basis yields have narrowed, he said, indicating that hedge funds have largely unwound the basis trade that paired spot ETF purchases with short futures. That means the current outflows are mainly driven by investors actively cutting their Bitcoin exposure, Sun said.

"If macro expectations do not improve, investors may shift from buying the dip to selling into rallies, creating additional overhead resistance on subsequent rebounds," he added.

"Recent Bitcoin ETF outflows and leveraged liquidations" have amplified the decline, Hathorn said. "Despite stronger Nvidia earnings, the market has struggled to stage a significant rebound, suggesting confidence remains fragile. A sustained recovery may require renewed ETF inflows and a more supportive interest-rate outlook."

Some traders have also pointed the finger at Anthropic's upcoming IPO for drawing money away from crypto, though analysts have disputed that the listing is draining crypto liquidity, attributing it instead to ETF outflows, forced selling and rising interest rates.

Traders see a 90.7% chance that the Fed will raise rates by a quarter point at its December 9 meeting, and a 9.3% chance of a half-point hike, according to CME FedWatch. The odds of a half-point move have risen from 6.5% a day earlier. Fed Governor Christopher Waller has called for an even bigger, half-point increase, unless policymakers signal another rise in January.

Hathorn said $64,000 is the immediate level to watch, followed by support around $62,000 and the psychological $60,000 mark. A sustained recovery above $66,000 to $68,000 could ease selling pressure, "but the broader trend remains bearish while lower highs persist," she said.

Onchain analytics firm Glassnode said in its weekly report on Tuesday that the crash had pushed investors’ realized losses to levels seen only near past market lows in 2018, 2020, 2022 and early 2023, a sign of capitulation. Bitcoin is now holding a dense block of recent buyers between $62,000 and $66,000, which grew by about 66,000 BTC during the two days of heaviest selling, Glassnode said. But a daily close below that block could set off a fast drop toward the June low of $58,500, and the Realized Price, the average price at which all Bitcoin last moved, at $53,700.

Traders on Decrypt Predict see a 43% chance that Bitcoin will fall to $60,000 at some point before the end of November, and a 12% chance that it will drop as low as $55,000. They give just a 2% chance that it will climb back to $82,500 this month.

There are some signs of support. About 1.1 million BTC, roughly 5.5% of supply, last changed hands at prices between $60,000 and $64,000, and that band has grown by more than 25,000 BTC in recent days, according to Neil Steinhardt, head of Nexo U.S., in a note shared with Decrypt Wednesday. A dense base of holders with costs near current prices "can act as a support zone, though it is not a floor," he wrote.

Bitcoin has also held up better than gold. The amount of gold one Bitcoin buys rose above its 200-day average this week, to about 17.1 ounces, around 40% above its March low, Steinhardt said.

#5129. Solana’s 2027 roadmap promises faster growth, but the market wants proof

Solana’s core developer, Anza, has unveiled its 2027 roadmap.

Structurally, the roadmap focuses on making Solana faster, more efficient, and capable of handling more activity. The network aims to double its compute capacity and cut the compute units needed for token account transactions by 80%.

It also plans to increase the number of accounts supported in each transaction from 64 to 96 and make it easier to run models fully on-chain.

Naturally, the question becomes whether Solana is preparing for its next growth phase. Interestingly, the previous major network upgrade was also performed by Anza.

This upgrade, called Alpenglow, brought down Solana’s finality time to 150ms from 12.8 seconds, making the network significantly faster.

The result? As the chart above shows, Solana processed over 10 billion transactions in October, keeping monthly activity above that level. However, more than halfway through November, the network has recorded just over 2 billion transactions.

That’s 5x lower than October’s total, suggesting that the recent spike in activity may be losing steam. Given this, it might be too early to expect any bull run in 2027.

In fact, SOL is currently down 20% in October, which indicates that the market hasn’t seen increased demand from improving fundamentals just yet.

So, what does it say about the recent “Anthropic-driven” momentum on Solana [SOL]?

SPCX was first to demonstrate how major IPOs can bring fresh trading activity to Solana.

The launch of SpaceX’s tokenized stock, SPCX, on Solana on the 12th of June brought significant activity to the network.

The token recorded $108 million in 24-hour on-chain trading volume shortly after launch and crossed 10,000 holders within six days, with cumulative trading volume exceeding $350 million.

Notably, a similar trend has emerged following the ANT IPO launch. As the chart below shows, Anthropic’s ANT has generated over $29 million in trading volume on Solana since launch across three issuers. Backpack’s token alone accounted for $26.8 million, or nearly 92% of the total.

This shows how major IPO launches are bringing fresh trading activity to Solana.

Adding to this, DeFiLlama data shows that Solana’s stablecoin market cap has risen nearly 3% in the past 24 hours, pointing to a fresh liquidity inflow after months of weakness.

However, the bigger picture remains mixed.

Despite the rise in on-chain activity and liquidity, SOL is still trading around $70. This suggests that the recent activity has yet to translate into stronger buying pressure.

For Solana’s 2027 roadmap to support a longer-term recovery, the network will therefore need to sustain this growth beyond short-term activity.

Anza’s 2027 roadmap aims to improve Solana’s speed, capacity, and overall network efficiency.

SPCX and ANT have boosted on-chain trading activity, but SOL’s price weakness suggests that stronger demand is still missing.

Home » Altcoins » Dozens of Seats Go Unclaimed At Donald Trump’s Memecoin Dinner

Presently, only 130 crypto whale wallets qualified for Trump’s fancy memecoin dinner at the golf club.

Just 130 crypto wallets secured seats for the November 22 TRUMP token holder dinner at Donald Trump’s Virginia golf club, leaving dozens of the 185 available places unclaimed. The Official Trump token was trading near record lows at the time of the close.

The event is designed to reward the largest holders, with the top 29 wallets also eligible for a VIP reception. Contest participants held roughly $8.6 million in tokens combined when the qualification period ended, a sharp drop in engagement from the project’s first holder dinner.

BREAKING: 🇺🇸 Trump will host an exclusive dinner for the top 185 $TRUMP holders this Sunday.The coin is down 99% from its peak. pic.twitter.com/NxizWHlrVg

Ranking was based on time-weighted holdings, which encouraged accumulation and retention through the window.

More than 5,000 eligible holders reportedly did not register. The leaderboard’s combined value represented only a small fraction of TRUMP’s roughly $268 million market capitalization.

TRUMP was trading around $0.95 in the latest reporting, down roughly 46% over the prior month after setting a record low near $0.896 on November 14. The token remains well below its peak, with one account describing it as down almost 99% from its high.

Large holders added to positions during the dip. Nansen data showed the top 100 wallets increased their combined holdings by 1.27% over 30 days, while a separate whale cohort expanded holdings by 26.63%. Exchange balances fell slightly over the same period.

Top-ranked winners risk losing VIP benefits if balances drop below specified levels before the event, and lower-ranked winners can forfeit their seat by selling more than half their qualifying balance. Those restrictions expire once the dinner is over.

Ahead of the 2025 dinner, 92 of 220 invited holders reportedly sold their entire positions before the event.

A Super Bowl-themed leaderboard planned for February 2027 may give some buyers a reason to stay involved, but it does not remove the immediate question of whether winners will take liquidity afterward.

#5126. Ethereum’s Glamsterdam delay reveals a troubling pattern behind its biggest network upgrades

An Ethereum Foundation researcher says the schedule underestimated how much there was to review. Core developers are weighing a December test.

Ethereum's Glamsterdam upgrade has slipped into 2027, exposing a growing disconnect between faster development and the network's ability to meet deadlines.

On Nov. 20, Ethereum Foundation researcher Toni Wahrstätter said the upgrade, which the foundation had targeted for the first half of 2026, cannot reach mainnet before mid-January 2027, after delays disrupted its testing schedule.

In a detailed assessment of the setback, Wahrstätter acknowledged that Ethereum developers had repeatedly underestimated how long major network upgrades would take, even as their productivity reached new highs.

“Nobody did a bad job, but I think we fooled ourselves, twice.”

His findings show that Glamsterdam was assigned the shortest development timeline in years despite being Ethereum's most ambitious upgrade by several measures.

According to Wahrstätter, monthly contributions to Ethereum's technical specifications have increased between twofold and 3.5-fold since 2024, reflecting a substantial acceleration in development activity.

The improvement has extended to testing. Glamsterdam completed 12 development networks, or devnets, in 160 days, compared with seven devnets over 285 days for Pectra, an earlier Ethereum upgrade.

However, Wahrstätter argued that the acceleration has created another problem: developers can now produce specifications, code and tests faster than their colleagues can review them and understand their implications.

That challenge has become more pronounced with Glamsterdam's unprecedented size. The upgrade contains approximately 6,080 lines of execution-layer specifications, compared with 2,318 for Prague, the previous record.

In a separate count of proposal specifications, Wahrstätter put two of Glamsterdam's most important changes, enshrined proposer-builder separation (ePBS) and block-level access lists (BALs), at approximately 11,900 and 9,300 lines, respectively. The other 16 proposals collectively represent about 3,600 lines.

The complexity is also reflected in EIP-8037, a proposal that changes how Ethereum charges for creating new blockchain state. Although its specifications contain roughly 1,700 lines, the proposal requires approximately 30,000 lines of tests, more than any other proposal included in the upgrade.

Together, this illustrates why faster code production has failed to produce a corresponding acceleration in network upgrades.

Indeed, Wahrstätter's historical analysis showed that every Ethereum upgrade since Dencun has taken more than 400 days from finalizing its scope to reaching mainnet. For context, the three most recent upgrades took between 433 and 475 days, even though their technical scope was smaller than Glamsterdam's.

Despite that record, Glamsterdam was given a development target of just 320 days, substantially shorter than the timelines achieved by previous upgrades.

Wahrstätter found that virtually every Ethereum upgrade with an announced target had missed its deadline. Fusaka was the exception, but only after developers removed Ethereum Object Format (EOF), a major component originally planned for inclusion.

Pectra similarly required developers to divide its original scope across separate upgrades.

Glamsterdam took a different approach. Developers kept adding proposals to successive testing environments while work on its two main components, ePBS and BALs, continued.

Unlike earlier upgrades, the team made no comparable reduction in scope to protect its development timeline.

Consequently, Glamsterdam reached public testing before its specifications had stabilized, creating additional work at a stage when developers would ordinarily be preparing for deployment.

Wahrstätter's analysis showed that Ethereum upgrades between Altair and Deneb recorded no specification changes after their first public testnet.

Pectra recorded two changes, while Fusaka recorded one. Glamsterdam registered 10 in just six weeks.

The difference also appeared in client development. Work on Pectra declined substantially after public testing began, whereas Glamsterdam-related activity increased 34% following its Sepolia activation, alongside a 25% rise in client commits.

Those late changes became particularly consequential after security researchers identified problems involving EIP-8037 and EIP-8038, which alter how Ethereum charges for certain operations.

The proposals could disrupt assumptions embedded in existing smart contracts, prompting developers to postpone Glamsterdam's Oct. 26 activation on the Hoodi testnet.

The setback has pushed Glamsterdam's expected interval between its first public testnet and mainnet activation beyond 100 days, compared with the 4- to 10-week window typical of previous upgrades, according to Wahrstätter.

During their Nov. 19 meeting, Ethereum developers tentatively targeted Dec. 16 or 17 for Hoodi testing, with mid-January 2027 emerging as the earliest possible mainnet date if the specification stays unchanged.

Wahrstätter argued that preventing further delays would require developers to base release targets on historical performance and set firm deadlines for dropping unfinished features and completing specifications before public testing begins.

He also questioned treating successful devnet deployments as evidence that proposals were sufficiently mature for inclusion in an upgrade. He said:

“I'm sure we can ship faster, but for that, we must ship smaller.”

The next decision comes Nov. 26, when Ethereum's core developers are expected to determine whether Glamsterdam can proceed with its proposed December Hoodi activation.

A further postponement would place additional pressure on a release schedule that has already extended well beyond its original target.

#5125. GameStop CEO Says Digital-Only Games Have ‘Hurt Consumers’ as GTA 6 Skips Discs

GameStop CEO Says Digital-Only Games Have ‘Hurt Consumers’ as GTA 6 Skips Discs

GameStop CEO Ryan Cohen has criticized video game publishers for abandoning physical discs, as Grand Theft Auto 6, one of the most anticipated games ever made, launches on Thursday as a digital download only.

"When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend," Cohen told Bloomberg. "Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it's also hurt GameStop."

Cohen declined to name specific companies, but Take-Two Interactive is releasing the $80 game only as a download, with retailers selling boxes containing download codes. Asked about presales, Cohen said: "It's a code in a box. I mean, we're selling a lot of it."

Take-Two declined to comment to Bloomberg.

The shift hits a core part of GameStop's business. Pre-owned and refurbished products made up 22% of the retailer's sales, about $171 million, in the quarter that ended August 1, down 32% from a year earlier, according to Bloomberg.

Cohen said he has spoken with publishers, who he argued benefit from limiting trade-ins because used copies compete with new sales. "They're taking away competition," he said.

Sony announced in July that it will stop producing physical discs for new PlayStation games in January 2028, a move experts have said will hit low-income gamers hardest. PlayStation founder Ken Kutaragi has dismissed the backlash as a "mentality issue," while an Infinity Ward veteran said publishers have pushed to cut discs since 2007.

Cohen said he has met with Rep. Ritchie Torres (D-NY), who is backing the Power to the Players Act, which would require gaming companies to give consumers ongoing access to the titles they buy. "A game that can be taken away the moment a company pulls the plug is not a purchase. It is a rental disguised as a sale," Torres said in October.

In Europe, the Stop Killing Games campaign gathered 1.3 million signatures for a European Citizens' Initiative calling for publishers to keep games playable after support ends.

The question of whether buyers own digital games has also reached the courts. Sony has argued in court that digital games can't be owned, prompting some in the crypto industry to pitch blockchain-based ownership as a fix.

Cohen's GameStop has also made bets beyond gaming. The company bought 4,710 BTC for more than $500 million in 2025, and in March moved all but one of them into a covered call strategy on Coinbase Prime to generate income. In May, after eBay rejected its takeover offer, GameStop sought shareholder approval to raise its authorized share count to 2.5 billion as it built a stake in the online marketplace.

#5124. 30K Bitcoin and A LOT of noise — It’s what a Tesla-SpaceX merger really means for crypto

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

“Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes.”

That’s what Elon Musk said about the idea to merge Tesla and SpaceX, back in October 2026.

Since then, however, it would seem that this somewhat fanciful idea has only accelerated. Over the last few weeks alone, both Tesla and SpaceX have constituted special exploratory committees consisting of independent directors.

Will it go through? Probably, yes. After all, despite the CEO of SpaceX and Tesla claiming that he is a “conflicted party,” his companies’ shareholders have often acceded to his wishes. That’s an opinion Walter Isaacson, author of “Elon Musk,” shares too.

Especially after the entrepreneur made his case by stating,

…there’s a lot of merit to combining the companies as we are pretty much in the Super Intelligence singularity.

Needless to say, such a merger will have some legal, regulatory, and financial implications. But what about the crypto sector?

Tesla, Inc., the automotive and clean energy company, holds 11,509 BTC valued at over $747 million right now. Similarly, SpaceX, the aerospace manufacturer, holds 18,712 BTC worth over $1.22 billion.

In simple terms, the merger will simply be a transaction that pools in digital assets owned by both these entities into a single balance sheet. This consolidation would allow the merged entity to hold 30,221 BTC in reserves.

Those are significant numbers. However, here’s where it’s also worth looking at the context and scale and the bigger picture.

Neither Tesla nor SpaceX are crypto companies. They are primarily tech manufacturing companies with valuations of $1.54 trillion and $1.89 trillion, respectively.

Yes, they have crypto holdings, but they aren’t significant enough for each individual entity to suggest that these are more than a passing interest and a diversification opportunity.

To put it in financial terms, for both Tesla and SpaceX, Bitcoin is a non-core balance sheet asset. For them, their BTC holdings are financially immaterial to their core CapEx. As Dr. Andrei Belonogov, Managing Partner at TechAccountingPro pointed out,

The size of treasuries is relatively small compared to the company’s debt maturities and non-cancellable commitments.

This will remain the case if the merger does go through. If and when it happens, the merged companies’ valuation would dwarf the value of its crypto holdings.

What about after, though? This is an important question because more often than not, non-core balance sheet assets go through a period of evaluation and restructuring and sometimes, disposal too to streamline operations and facilitate profitability.

Could this happen to the aforementioned Bitcoin holdings then? Well, that’s always a possibility. However, recent history suggests the odds are low.

Consider the purchase and sale history of both these companies, for instance. The last time Tesla sold any of its Bitcoin holdings was back in 2022. Since then, it has bought additional BTC while also holding on to the stash it already had.

Similarly, SpaceX last sold any of its holdings back in 2024. In the two years since, the aerospace manufacturer has only bought Bitcoin. Specifically, over 10K BTC in May 2026.

Now, it’s up for debate how much input the “conflicted party,” Musk, had in any of these sales or purchases. However, it is safe to assume that, given the consistencies between the two boardrooms so far, that will remain the case after the merger too.

What about later though? Well, MetaWin COO Rory Cartwright told AMBCrypto,

The merger doesn’t necessarily mean a sell-off or any spike in price. What it will do, however, is put a roughly $2bn position into a single company’s balance sheet. Bitcoin can be especially volatile, so that may make some investors seasick

Will the merged entity enjoy the same degree of flexibility Tesla and SpaceX enjoyed individually when it comes to crypto sales and purchases though? According to Kevin Constantine, Senior Associate at Caldwell Law,

Protections could become relevant to cryptocurrency holdings, particularly if management’s ability to purchase, liquidate, or transfer Bitcoin raised concerns about the companies’ valuations or the treatment of shareholders.

The fact that both Tesla and SpaceX refused to sell their Bitcoin in 2026, a year that has been particularly bearish for the crypto-sector, is testament to the confidence they have in this asset. It is also a sign of institutional conviction.

After the merger, the merged entity will have the potential to be the sixth-largest corporate Bitcoin holder in the world. Only behind crypto-native firms or treasury-focused players like MicroStrategy and Metaplanet. All while Bitcoin remains its non-core balance sheet asset.

That, more than anything, will be confirmation of Bitcoin’s value as a corporate treasury asset. That might not sound like much on paper, but that is still VERY bullish news.

What could be even better though? According to Chris Mack, CTO at Quote.Trade,

If Musk came out publicly bullish on Bitcoin and crypto, that would change things. Investors would start paying attention to whether he plans to buy more or make crypto part of the business.

That’s not all either. As it stands, both Tesla and SpaceX have significant investments in scaling AI infrastructure. This is likely to continue after the merger, with more capital and resources allocated to AI compute and energy grids.

In a very indirect way, such investments could have a positive impact on AI-focused crypto tokens like RENDER, TAO, and NEAR, especially in the long run.

At the time of writing, reports seemed to suggest that Tesla and SpaceX are targeting a potential deal announcement by January 2027 or even as early as December 2026.

That’s an accelerated timeline, one that may or may not have anything to do with Democrats’ victory in the midterm elections. Democrats, many of whom are also planning to probe Elon Musk’s corporate ties.

Even outside the political element, though, it probably won’t be all sunshine and roses. After all, this is a merger between a major U.S. defense and Starlink contractor with an automative company with a significant manufacturing and sales footprint in China.

The regulatory and legal questions involved alone will be a nightmare.

Will crypto be an irrelevant factor then? Speaking to AMBCrypto, Constantine claimed,

As it stands, a lot of things are still up in the air. It’s too early to say how Tesla and SpaceX will quell national security concerns while juggling regulatory challenges with this merger. That’s the unpredictable part.

What is not unpredictable is what will happen to their cryptos and the crypto sector at large if this merger goes through. Relatively speaking, that is.

#5123. Kraken Suffers Temporary Glitch Allowing Users to Buy Bitcoin for $16,900

Bitcoin reportedly became available at a massive discount on Kraken after a sharp dislocation in Kraken's dollar trading markets.

Users reported being able to purchase BTC for as little as 24,250 CAD, equivalent to $16,900 at that time.

Apparently, the incident has only affected the BTC/CAD trading pair on the platform, although some users claim the disruption appeared across several CAD markets.

The cause the glitch is still unclear, while the reported transactions are yet to be verified.

The incident might have involved thin liquidity problem in Kraken's CAD order books.

Large sell orders reportedly overwhelmed available buy orders, leaving insufficient demand to absorb the selling pressure.

According to some accounts, at one point about 20 BTC was being sold every 15 minutes, causing the imbalance to push BTC price against CAD further down.

One such transaction resulted in BTC price at around C$24,250, or $16,900. Compared with Bitcoin trading between $57,000-$58,000, the discount amounted to a staggering 71%. Other users reported BTC briefly trading around $27,000.

Kraken's status page continued to show its systems as operational during the incident. No official explanation from the exchange was available at the time of writing.

The reported dislocation highlights the risks associated with trading in markets with limited liquidity. When an order book lacks sufficient buy-side depth, even relatively large sell orders can cause prices to move sharply away from the broader market.

On Friday, Bitcoin price dropped below $60,000. At some point, it fell 5.10% to $55,830, the lowest level since September 2024.

Liquidations on crypto exchanges reached $1.57 billion over 24 hours on Nov. 20.

According to CoinGlass, 265,525 traders were liquidated over 24 hours, and long positions accounted for $1.43 billion of the total.

Bitcoin saw $554.28 million in liquidations, and 91.3% of that amount came from long positions. Ethereum (ETH) fell below $1,700 on Nov. 20, and ETH traders saw $331.08 million in liquidations.

Binance accounted for 45.8% of all liquidations, and the largest single order was also on Binance: an $11.98 million ETH/USDT long position that was liquidated at $1,638.78.

#5122. Ripple ETF Investors Hold On, But XRP Buyers Go Missing

Home » Trendsetter News » Ripple ETF Investors Hold On, But XRP Buyers Go Missing

XRP ETF assets fell 31.6% despite modest redemptions, suggesting a lack of fresh demand, not a buyer exodus.

Ripple’s XRP-linked ETF assets fell 31.6% from September 30 through the Friday cited in the video, compared with a 20.2% decline for Bitcoin funds. Yet redemptions remained modest.

Dana Love, PhD, a popular market analyst examining ETF flows and corporate filings, argues that missing buyers, not an investor stampede, help explain the XRP’s deeper slide this month.

The XRP coin traded at $0.967 this Friday morning, following a last Friday low of $0.89.

Dana Love’s central claim: Bitcoin-related selling is weighing on XRP, while demand from XRP funds and a closely watched treasury company has failed to provide much support.

According to the figures presented, cumulative net inflows into XRP ETFs slipped from $1.809 billion on October 29 to $1.789 billion on Monday. That leaves roughly 98.9% of cumulative net inflows intact, despite the sharp decline in fund assets.

But November through that Monday brought no positive daily net flows. “Nobody is running for the exits,” the analyst says, “but nobody new was walking in.”

Bitcoin ETFs, meanwhile, recorded roughly $2.34 billion in November outflows through the same period. Monday’s $8 million inflow interrupted the selling, although the analyst cautions that one positive session does not establish a reversal.

The distinction matters: limited XRP ETF redemptions do not establish that XRP holders across the entire market are refusing to sell. Nor does a decline in fund assets measure withdrawals alone; falling token prices also reduce those balances.

Dana Love also questions Evernorth, the XRP treasury company whose October 14 release said it would “accumulate and deploy” XRP into institutional strategies beginning in the fourth quarter of 2026.

The video estimates that Evernorth had about $111 million in cash, including subsequent warrant proceeds, and says its shares still traded above estimated underlying asset value.

That could support further fundraising, although the company had not announced additional purchases in the period discussed.

Silence is not proof of inactivity. The analyst explicitly acknowledges that Evernorth may be buying without announcing every transaction.

For investors, the useful distinction is between broader market relief and renewed XRP-specific market demand.

Sustained Bitcoin ETF inflows would suggest selling pressure is easing; XRP inflows arriving independently, or a disclosed Evernorth purchase, would offer stronger evidence that XRP has found buyers of its own.

#5121. Kraken says trades stand after Bitcoin sold at $24,250 Canadian

Kraken said heavy selling drove its Canadian-dollar markets below prices elsewhere. Its Bitcoin pair climbed back above C$80,000 by early afternoon.

Bitcoin hit C$24,250 on Kraken’s Canadian-dollar market on Saturday, Nov. 21. The next 15-minute trading interval came within C$1.40 of that low. Kraken said executed trades would stand after heavy selling pushed its Canadian-dollar pairs below prices elsewhere.

The C$24,250 low was about 71% below the Canadian-dollar conversion on CryptoSlate’s Bitcoin price page at 09:40 UTC. The comparison puts an earlier Kraken trade alongside a later reference value. CryptoSlate displayed a price of US$57,809 and a converted value of C$82,708 at that check.

Kraken’s Canadian-dollar pair had already reached C$61,880 during the 15 minutes starting at 21:00 UTC on Friday. The trading intervals beginning at 06:00 and 07:00 UTC Saturday reached lows of C$50,000 and C$33,750, respectively.

The interval starting at 08:00 UTC opened at C$32,000, ranged from C$24,250 to C$49,999 and ended back at C$32,000. Kraken recorded 976 trades totaling about 22.38 BTC across those 15 minutes. How much Bitcoin changed hands at the lowest price remains unclear.

The next interval reached C$24,251.40 before closing at C$37,000. Kraken’s 09:40 UTC ticker still showed C$24,250 as the 24-hour low. The best bid was C$40,900 and the best ask was C$42,557. Kraken reported a high of C$88,964 and volume of about 658.51 BTC for the rolling 24-hour window. The bid and ask show where buyers and sellers were quoting at the time of the check.

Canadian dollars per Bitcoin. Each label gives the start of a selected 15-minute interval in UTC.

In the 09:40 UTC ticker, Kraken’s USD/CAD last price was C$0.7304 per U.S. dollar. Multiplying the exchange’s BTC/USD last price of about US$57,796 by that rate gives about C$42,214 per Bitcoin. That was close to C$42,557, the last price Kraken reported for its BTC/CAD pair in the same response.

The comparison shows how different the prices looked using Kraken’s own currency markets. A U.S. dollar traded for fewer Canadian dollars on Kraken, so using Kraken’s rate in place of the broader market conversion brought the implied Bitcoin price much closer to the direct CAD trade. The last trades in the three markets may have occurred at different times. The calculation gives an indicative price, and any actual order would depend on the price and quantity available at execution.

If momentum persists, XRP might be at risk of falling below the $0.7 mark as investor confidence is rapidly fading.

#5119. Binance Wins $6.5B Freezing Order Over Hack That Can Be Served via the Blockchain

Binance Wins $6.5B Freezing Order Over Hack That Can Be Served via the Blockchain

Binance has secured a $6.5 billion worldwide freezing order against the hackers behind last month's attack on the exchange, which the FBI has blamed on North Korea.

The injunction was issued by the courts of the Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) against the unknown perpetrators, Binance's lawyers at Gibson Dunn confirmed, according to City AM.

The order breaks new legal ground. It can be served directly via the blockchain, and market participants will be notified of a "living list" of 26,000 wallet addresses identified as holding stolen assets, Gibson Dunn partner Kendall Day said. That will enable "those assets to be frozen rapidly even as they are laundered at pace," Day said.

Binance has also secured proprietary injunctions and delivery-up orders, including against parties holding frozen assets who are not accused of wrongdoing, according to City AM. Decrypt has reached out to Gibson Dunn for comment.

"We will continue using every lawful tool available to trace, freeze and recover stolen assets, support our partners in returning funds where possible, and keep those assets out of the hands of the attackers," Dugan Bliss, Binance's deputy general counsel, said in a statement reported by Bloomberg.

The FBI has attributed the October 29 hack to TraderTraitor, a group linked to North Korea, which has denied involvement. The attackers gained access after an engineer was phished through a fake job offer, according to Bloomberg. The Secret Service has joined the FBI's investigation.

About $2.85 billion in funds connected to the hack has been frozen, including by Ripple and World Liberty Financial, according to Bloomberg. Stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle froze $2.7 billion shortly after the attack, and the Justice Department said last week it had obtained court authorization to seize or restrain $1.2 billion of that.

The hackers have used thousands of wallets and multiple blockchains to launder the rest, and wallets linked to the hack began moving Ethereum again this week after two weeks of inactivity.

Binance has said it fully covered the $6.3 billion in customer assets affected and absorbed the losses itself.

On the 1st of October 2025, entrepreneur and angel investor Naval Ravikant posted on X that,

Bitcoin is insurance against fiat. Zcash is insurance against Bitcoin.

Neither of the latter two tokens has managed to regain the highs they made back then.

Meanwhile, ZEC reached $1,700. The altcoin’s correction in recent months back below $1,000 has sparked bearish short-term sentiment, even though it was still trading above the previous year’s peak.

Sophisticated on-chain analysis can still narrow down to the 16 possibilities over multiple “hops”, or intermediate payments or asset transfers along a transaction trail.

Monero’s Full Chain Membership Proofs++ (FCMP++) eliminates the need for decoys. It replaces rings by providing zero-knowledge membership proofs across the entire blockchain output set. In other words, it mathematically proves that the spent XMR belongs to the Monero blockchain, making every previous output created part of the decoy set.

A mainnet activation date has not been confirmed for the FCMP++ and Carrot, the addressing protocol and wallet key hierarchy upgrade designed for the FCMP++ network upgrade. AMBCrypto reported that zkSecurity’s audit of FCMP++ was “complete, zero-knowledge, and sound”.

Using zero-knowledge cryptography, private ZEC balances and transactions are tracked in shielded pools. Zcash has five of these shielded pools, as well as its transparent pool. Once funds are inside, the older pools can not be shut down, but can be made spend-only.

The Ironwood (NU6.3) upgrade was launched on the 28th of July, 2026, addressing the Orchard “infinity” bug found in May. It also introduced a new shielded pool and restricted the Orchard pool. Funds exiting Orchard must now pass through Zcash’s turnstile, for supply integrity verification, to enter Ironwood.

The NU7 upgrade implemented in November aims to reduce block processing times by 67%, from 75 seconds to 25 seconds. It also reduced the wallet scanning workload required to perform private payments.

When transactions are shielded in some form, anti-money laundering (AML) tracing is hindered or prevented. This brings strict regulatory restrictions on shielded transactions, as they require visibility in fund flows to prevent illicit financing.

The latter argues that oversight is a necessity to prevent serious crimes and to detect and disrupt illicit activity.

Selective disclosure, such as in Zcash, Midnight, or using Identity Frameworks in Ethereum, can achieve this by sharing transaction details without revealing the entire financial history.

Zero-knowledge compliance is another approach that can prove that a transaction meets certain criteria, without exposing other relevant details.

Crypto exchange Binance has issued a "one-letter" security warning to crypto users, urging them to carefully check website addresses before logging into their accounts. According to Binance, a fake site can be just one letter off.

A post on X by the crypto exchange pointed out that a small difference in a website URL, sometimes just one letter, can lead users to visit fake websites impersonating legitimate platforms.

"Sometimes the biggest red flag is just one letter," Binance wrote.

Sometimes the biggest red flag is just one letter. Before you log in, double-check the URL. If you’re still not sure, use our official verification tool below 👇 https://t.co/HT068SANmn https://t.co/pBOQeU8GmC

The exchange advised users to double-check URLs before entering their login credentials. It also encouraged anyone uncertain about a website's authenticity to use Binance's official verification tool to confirm whether the URL belongs to the platform.

The Binance Verify platform allows crypto users to stay safe from scammers, as they can enter a URL, email address, phone number, Telegram account, or social media account to check if the source is verified and officially from Binance.

Impersonation scams are quietly growing across the crypto space, with one of the most troubling tactics seen being the deepfake: lifelike, AI-generated impersonations of crypto executives and employees soliciting money on video calls that look and sound real enough to make anyone hesitate. The personas are fabricated, but the sophistication is genuine.

Every day, people are contacted by impersonators using the names, likenesses, and even job titles of crypto personnel, including Binance staff, to solicit investments or financial transactions via WhatsApp, Telegram, and other channels.

Binance stated that scammers prey on people's growing interest in investing and digital finance and on their trust, often masquerading as its employees or executives to exploit its credibility.

With advances in AI and deepfake technology, they can create personas that look and sound real. Crypto users are therefore urged to beware of unsolicited advice or "special opportunities" and to refrain from clicking on unknown links or URLs.

#5115. US Treasury sells $15 billion in first nine-day cash bill auction since 2008

Buyers are due to pay on Nov. 24 and get repaid on Dec. 3. Treasury had flagged a possible short-term bill and held $891 billion in cash on auction day.

The U.S. Treasury auctioned $15 billion of nine-day cash management bills on Nov. 19, its first sale at that exact term since July 2008. The bills are scheduled to settle Nov. 24 and mature Dec. 3, putting the borrowing across the turn of the month.

Treasury had already flagged a possible short bill in its November financing plan. Its operating cash balance on auction day was within the range it had recorded in 2026. The proceeds were due when the bill settled five days later, so the auction-day balance gives a snapshot of Treasury’s cash before the new borrowing arrived.

The sale reopened a bill first issued on June 4. Investors could buy more of the same security, which kept its Dec. 3 maturity date. Treasury reported a high discount rate of 3.91% and a bid-to-cover ratio of 3.97. The ratio measures the face value of accepted and rejected offers Treasury counted, about $60 billion, against the just over $15 billion it awarded.

Treasury auctions cash management bills as needed to meet short-term financing needs. A recent sale ran one day longer. On Oct. 22, Treasury auctioned $25 billion of ten-day bills at a 3.93% high discount rate. Those bills were issued Oct. 26 and matured Nov. 5.

Before the November sale, Treasury’s previous nine-day auction was July 21, 2008, according to its historical auction records. It offered $9 billion at that sale, with a July 22 issue date and July 31 maturity.

Short bills remained in use. The legacy auction series records 29 cash management bill sales with terms of ten days or less after the July 2008 sale, through December 2025. The updated series includes the October and November 2026 auctions.

In its Nov. 4 quarterly refunding statement, Treasury said it might issue a short-dated bill around the end of November for cash management. It announced the offering on Nov. 18 and released the results the next day. The auction documents gave investors the dates for paying Treasury and getting repaid. They identified no specific federal expenses tied to the borrowing.

In a Nov. 20 post on X, @0xCVYH likened the sale to an overdraft, said Treasury’s cash had grown tight and argued that the borrowing would help cover end-of-month expenses. The auction schedule confirms that the borrowing spans month-end. The cash data offer a separate check on how unusual Treasury’s balance was at the time.

The Daily Treasury Statement put the Treasury General Account, the government’s operating cash account, at $891.223 billion at the Nov. 19 close, down from $892.310 billion the day before. Across Treasury’s daily balance series through Nov. 19, the 2026 low was $686.969 billion on April 9 and the high was $1.05253 trillion on Oct. 27. Nov. 19 was the latest close available as of Nov. 21. That snapshot gives a sense of scale. Assessing the pressure on Treasury’s cash also requires knowing when receipts and payments are due.

#5113. Morning Minute: Google’s Newest AI Model Tops Benchmarks Ahead of Anthropic IPO

Morning Minute: Google’s Newest AI Model Tops Benchmarks Ahead of Anthropic IPO

Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.

Google shipped Gemini 4 Neon on Wednesday, its fourth frontier model release in three weeks, and on the eve of the heavily anticipated Anthropic IPO.

This isn’t just a normal model release. For one, it’s incredibly good. Neon posts 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index against 59 for Claude Opus 5.5 and 57 for GPT-6.2 Sol. It takes the Vals Index at 70.9%, AutomationBench at 56.3% against Opus 5.5’s 42.5%, and GraphWalks long-context retrieval at 95.2% against Opus 5.5’s 66.8%.

Beyond just the outperformance, Google has been releasing at a pace nobody else is matching. It dropped Argon in mid-October. Carbon on October 28. Hydrogen last week. Google owns its silicon, its data centers, and its distribution, and it is using all three to iterate faster than labs that rent compute. And it has some speculating that Google has already achieved RSI (recursive self-improvement), the final step ahead of super intelligence.

So Google has caught up at the top of the AI race. Just in time for the ANT IPO.

Anthropic will be priced at $83, 6.4% above the top of its $70 to $78 range, valuing the company around $1.5 trillion fully diluted. On the 825 million shares in the original terms, that’s roughly $68.5 billion raised, and about $94.5 billion counting the separate $26 billion private placement from its compute suppliers. It trades Thursday on Nasdaq as ANT. Notably, ANT has been trading on Hyperliquid in the $90-$100 range for the past week but popped to $105 this morning.

The valuation math is a 55% step-up from the $965 billion May round and about 25% below the $2 trillion Anthropic was reportedly chasing in September. Revenue ran $33.2 billion through nine months against $2.5 billion a year earlier, a 13x increase. Annualize that and $1.5 trillion is roughly 34 times sales.

That’s a steep raise given the macro backdrop and the Fed calling for more hikes for longer. AI stocks have been shaky over the past month and even moreso since Jensen Huang left Nvidia. Not the most confident market headed into the 2nd $1T+ IPO of the year.

So what does it mean for today’s price action? Personally, I expect a pop to the $95-$105 level that Hyperliquid has been pricing out for weeks, and it likely sees a spike higher. But there will be massive volatility, and it’s very likely to trade under that $83 level over the coming days and weeks. Especially given the new (surprise) headwinds from Google with its outperforming model.

We will find out soon enough. Good luck to everyone trading it today.
